question: What does the matrix stage of a TrueHD object substream multiply, and how much of it has to be?
method: Timers around the stages of the TrueHD decoder, in a throwaway build, gave the shares of the thread that decodes the widest presentation of a 16-channel stream. Counters in another gave what the matrix stage multiplies over the widest presentations of the six object streams of the comparison. A matrix of a 0x31EC substream has a delta for every coefficient and is summed with both; where its deltas are all zero the second sum is zero whatever the samples are, and it is left out. What that is worth was measured inside one binary, built for the purpose with a switch that sums every matrix with its deltas as before: both ways turn and turn about, nine runs each, bound to the fast cores. The binary of the change was also measured against the binary of main (`tools/bench.py --compare`, five runs). That no sample changed was looked for over the corpus (`tools/old_new.py --decode-all`, every presentation of every stream) and in the campaign of evidence 22. The streams are media and are not in the repository.

where_the_time_of_the_thread_that_decode.how: timers in a throwaway build of main, the decode of the widest presentation of a 16-channel stream, the least of five runs; the timers cost time themselves

what_the_matrix_stage_multiplies.how: counters in a throwaway build, the decode of the widest presentation of six object streams
what_the_matrix_stage_multiplies.reading: a matrix has a delta for every coefficient, so the deltas were half of the products; the coefficients themselves are mostly set, and nothing is to be had from leaving out the ones that are zero

the_change_inside_one_binary.how: one binary with a switch in its environment; the time of a command that leaves the deltas of a still matrix out over its time summing every matrix with them, medians of nine runs

the_binary_of_the_change_against_the_bin.reading: no command that runs the matrix stage on an object substream is slower, and all but 1 of 24 are faster by more than the spread of their runs. The commands the tool calls slower run none of what changed: they are presentations of six and eight channels, whose matrices have no deltas, and they differ between the two binaries by what evidence 39 found the placing of this stage to be worth

three_ways_of_writing_it.how: the decode of the object presentation of four streams, bound to the fast cores, nine runs each: the binary of main (`base`), the sums written in the loop with the test of whether a matrix moves beside them (`inline`), that test in a function of its own (`helper`), and a loop for each kind of substream (`parted`)
three_ways_of_writing_it.reading: the three are within three per cent of one another on every stream, which is within what the placing of the stage is worth. The one with the function was taken, because the function can be tested by itself, and the function is forced in line, which the kernels of the fixture put within two per cent of not forcing it

the_kernels.reading: the fixture has an object presentation of twelve channels, a quarter of whose matrices move; its other presentations run none of what changed

reading: The matrix stage is 43.8 per cent of the decode of a 16-channel presentation, and half of what it multiplied were deltas, which are zero for 82.8 to 100.0 per cent of the matrices applied. Leaving those out, the object presentation decodes in 88.4 to 93.8 per cent of the time and `verify --decode` in 95.2 to 97.5, inside one binary, on six object streams; no sample of any presentation of any stream of the corpus changes.
